items.title: SCJC publicly admonishes Municipal Judge Don G. Adams for dangerous-dog case failures
items.source: The Hawk’s Eye / SCJC official order
items.summary: The State Commission on Judicial Conduct issued a public admonition (order dated Oct. 7, 2026) to Judge Don G. Adams of Sunrise Beach Village (Llano County) for failing to hold a dangerous-dog hearing within the required 10 days, failing to transfer the case or allow a requested jury trial, and failing to timely handle a recusal motion. During the delayed hearing he held the attorney in contempt and had her taken to jail. Adams has continued serving as municipal judge in other Hill Country cities.
items.quality: High (official SCJC Public Admonition order and detailed reporting)

items.title: Bexar County DA’s office withdraws recusal request in Neil Calfas prosecution
items.summary: Prosecutors withdrew the Oct. 27 motion by Bexar County Criminal District Attorney Joe Gonzales to recuse his office from the trafficking and solicitation case against defense attorney Neil Calfas. The original motion cited 2018 campaign contributions, a prior business relationship, and Calfas representing other defendants. The withdrawal leaves the office in place for the remainder of Gonzales’ term; next hearing Dec. 9 on discovery.
items.quality: High (KSAT and San Antonio Express-News coverage of the hearing and withdrawal)

items.title: Former Midland County Judge Terry Johnson enters pretrial diversion; resigns effective Dec. 16
items.summary: Former Midland County Judge Terry Johnson entered a one-year pretrial diversion agreement on Nov. 13 to resolve charges of misuse of official information, fraudulent use of identifying information, and abuse of official capacity arising from a Facebook post that included a resident's personal data. Upon successful completion the charges will be dismissed. Separately, he agreed to resign effective Dec. 16 and repaid $50,000 in salary following an SCJC suspension and civil removal suit.
items.quality: High (District Attorney statement and local reporting of court agreements)

items.title: SCJC issues Public Warning to Harris County Judge Nathan Milliron for undignified conduct
items.source: State Commission on Judicial Conduct (official order)
items.summary: The SCJC publicly warned Judge Nathan Milliron of the 215th District Court (Harris County) for failing to be patient, dignified and courteous in multiple interactions (including a viral courtroom exchange with an IT worker, threats to have an attorney cuffed, and removing a party from the courtroom) and for failing to afford an opportunity to be heard on a proposed order. The order was issued November 5, 2026, following the Commission's October meeting.

items.title: Dallas federal Judge Ada Brown under investigation for misconduct; panel finds she abandoned her post
items.summary: A Fifth Circuit judicial committee concluded U.S. District Judge Ada Brown is unable to perform her duties due to a mental condition, citing abandonment of her post, hostile treatment of judges and staff including racial insults, habitual delays, and refusal to cooperate with the investigation. She was ordered to undergo a psychiatric exam and had cases reassigned. The investigation remains ongoing.
items.quality: High (Dallas Morning News reporting based on official Fifth Circuit Judicial Council orders and committee findings)

items.title: Bexar County DA Joe Gonzales seeks recusal from Neil Calfas case citing potential conflict
items.summary: Bexar County Criminal District Attorney Joe Gonzales filed a motion to recuse himself and his office from prosecuting defense attorney Neil Calfas on solicitation and human trafficking charges. Gonzales cited campaign contributions from Calfas in 2018, a prior landlord-tenant relationship, and Calfas currently representing other defendants against the office, creating an appearance of impropriety.
items.quality: High (KSAT and San Antonio Express-News coverage of filed motion)

items.title: Rains County Justice of the Peace suspended without pay; State Bar reports disciplinary actions
items.summary: The State Bar of Texas monthly report notes that Rains County JP Robert Jenkins Franklin was suspended without pay following an aggravated perjury indictment related to testimony in a child support hearing. The suspension is by the State Commission on Judicial Conduct pending resolution of the charges. Fourteen attorneys were also disciplined in the same reporting period.
items.quality: High (Law.com reporting on official State Bar / SCJC actions)

items.title: Texas Rangers reviewing allegations against Guadalupe County Judge Kyle Kutscher
items.summary: The Texas Rangers confirmed they are reviewing allegations that Guadalupe County Judge Kyle Kutscher violated state law in connection with his family's pending property sale to a data center developer while participating in related county matters. The sheriff referred the information; parallel civil litigation alleges conflicts and Open Meetings issues. Kutscher has said he will not seek re-election.
items.quality: High (local reporting confirming DPS/Rangers receipt of referral)
